svg.title: RIEMANN R8 — Galois representations: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 8 in one poster: its 38 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-galois-reps-polarized, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: This chapter proves thm-galois-reps-polarized: every polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representation π of GL_a over a CM field has an l-adic Galois representation, with the Hodge–Tate weights read off π and with Weil–Deligne representations that match the local parameters of π wherever these are determined (rem-local-parameters-weak). The outline needs it in thm-grh-from-galois: these representations bound the Tate–Shafarevich groups of chap-sha and enter the families of chap-families. The statement is a weak form of the theorem of Harris–Taylor, Shin, Chenevier–Harris, Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor and Caraiani. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

A → B: the proof of B uses A (the arrow takes A's colour)
A ⇢ B: the proof of B names A without listing it as a use (dashed)
Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the statement, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines (four on a short card). The footer gives its file and
line in the mirror and the other declarations.
The line in italics is the blueprint's statement, and the bullets are its proof, paragraph by paragraph, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges. A proof use outside the chapter is counted, not drawn. Rows: a card's row is one above the highest card whose proof uses it, or higher
where that makes room; a card sits under the cards that use it where it can. A short card shows four lines of the signature and one paragraph of the proof.

text.tspan: What the chapter uses from outside, and what uses it

svg.text: The chapter's proofs and statements use 170 results outside it, 163 from chap-literature, 6 from architecture, 1 from chap-theta.
Used most thm-hasse-norm-quadratic (9), thm-de-rham-abelian-schemes (7), lem-hodge-filtration-abelian-scheme (7), thm-dual-abelian-scheme (7), thm-bz-finiteness (6),
Used by other chapters thm-galois-reps-csd-above-l (17), thm-labesse-base-change (9), thm-galois-reps-polarized-cuspidal (7), thm-base-change-unitary (6),

text.tspan: Named in a proof, not listed as a use

svg.text: The proof texts of these statements name a result of the chapter that their uses lists leave
out. Either the Lean theorem takes it as a hypothesis, or the blueprint's edge resolution
missed it; the diagram cannot tell which.

text.tspan: 2 · The chapter, from its leaves down to its theorem

svg.text: 14 rows. Section by section the chapter runs: 1. From odd rank and theta lifts to all polarized pairs (3); 2. Local-global compatibility at ramified places (3); 3. Geometric Galois representations in odd rank (2); 4. Hecke eigenspaces in etale cohomology (9); 5. Kuga-Sato varieties over unitary Shimura varieties (4); 6. Integral models of compact unitary Shimura varieties (7); 7. Base change between definite unitary groups and GL(n) (7); 8. The forms used by the families (2). The cards keep that order within a row

text.tspan: A bound for Hecke operators in base change

svg.text: ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (π : Submodule ℂ (UA E n → ℂ)), IsAutRepU π →
∀ (S T : Finset (Pl E)) (F₀ : Frame0 hR π S) (F : RunFrame F₀
Let E be a CM field with E/E^+ unramified, n ≥ 1, and U an automorphic representation of the
definite unitary group U_n over E^+. For finite sets S, T of places, the families of Hecke
operators built from U on spaces of automorphic forms of fixed level satisfy a uniform bound,
used to read off Satake parameters in the proof of base change. It is not clear exactly what the
bounded quantities are; we read them as the entries of Hecke operators in bases adapted to
the torus at the places of T.
We read the proof as a comparison of trace formulas, with test functions from wave kernels at
the archimedean places (thm-wave-kernels-gln-c) and the fundamental lemma at
unramified places (thm-jacquet-rallis-fundamental-lemma); the Hasse norm theorem is
also used. We have not unfolded it.

text.tspan: Fixed points of Hecke correspondences on Kuga–Sato

svg.text: Let G be as in thm-kuga-sato-unitary-shimura, over ℂ, with levels N | N', and let h ∈
G(A_f) be such that the Hecke operator of h is supported on regular elements. Compose the
Hecke correspondence of h on the k-th Kuga–Sato variety with translation by sections
alpha_1, …, alpha_k of mathcal O_F, all non-zero and divisible by 2. …
Coincidence points of a Hecke correspondence are abelian varieties with an isogeny of the
given type, hence CM points. thm-coincidence-points-cm counts them and computes their
tangent action, and the translations by the alpha_s act on the fibres of the Kuga–Sato variety.

Kummer sequence and the Picard group of a normal proper model, kills cohomology classes

text.tspan: Base change from definite unitary groups

svg.text: Let E be a CM field with E/E^+ unramified at the finite places. Every automorphic
representation of a definite unitary group in n variables over E^+ has a weak base change to
GL_n(A_E). The base change is an isobaric sum of conjugate-self-dual discrete automorphic
representations of groups GL_(n_i)(A_E), compatible with the local base change at split
places, at unramified inert places and at infinity.
We read the proof as Labesse's comparison of the trace formula of the definite unitary group
with the twisted trace formula of GL_n over E. …

text.tspan: Base change from unitary groups to GL(n)

svg.text: Let E be a CM field such that E is unramified over its maximal totally real subfield E^+ at every
finite place, and n ≥ 1. Every automorphic representation π of a definite unitary group in n
variables over E^+, split by E, has a base change to GL_n(A_E): there are a partition n = N_1
+ … + N_c with all N_i > 0, discrete automorphic representations Pi_i of GL_(N_i)(A_E)
that are conjugate self-dual, and local components sigma_(i,w) such that: at a place where π
is unramified, the product of the sigma_(i,w) is spherical, and at inert places its Satake
parameter is the base change of …
Start from the isobaric base change of thm-base-change-unitary, which gives the local
component of π as a subquotient of the product of the local components of the Pi_i. These
are unitarisable, so their product is irreducible, and the subquotient is the whole product. …

text.tspan: Kuga–Sato varieties over unitary Shimura varieties

svg.text: Let G be a unitary group of odd rank n over a CM field F, of signature (1, n-1) at one infinite
place and (0, n) at the others, attached to a PEL datum of the kind used by Harris and Taylor
with compact Shimura varieties. For k ≥ 0 let the Kuga–Sato variety of level N be the k-fold
fibre power of the universal abelian scheme over the Shimura variety of level N. Then: the
Shimura varieties have models over F, and for every k the Kuga–Sato varieties with their Hecke
correspondences form a Hecke tower (thm-galois-reps-hecke-eigenspaces): smooth,
The integral models of the Shimura varieties come from
thm-unitary-shimura-integral-models: a smooth quasi-projective moduli scheme,
proper because the datum is compact. Fibre powers of the universal abelian scheme are
smooth and projective, and the Hecke correspondences are finite étale. …

text.tspan: 3 · The argument in the chapter's own words, section by section

svg.text: The first paragraph of each section's introduction in the blueprint, in the chapter's order, with the statements each section holds. Abridged where marked with ….

text.tspan: 1. From odd rank and theta lifts to all polarized pairs

svg.text: This section reduces thm-galois-reps-polarized to two inputs (
sec-gal-odd-rank and the non-vanishing of theta lifts from definite unitary groups (
thm-theta-lift-nonvanishing, after Rallis and Li). From the odd-rank representations we
cut out a piece of the right dimension, reach all weights by congruences and a limit, in the
style of Chenevier, of pseudo-representations, isolate even-rank representations between two
theta lifts to odd rank, and descend from GL_a to unitary groups. The ramified places are left
sec-gal-assembly gives Galois representations compatible at the unramified places; this
section adds the ramified places that def-galois-reps-polarized asks about (
thm-local-global-ramified). Compatibility first extends to principal series from characters
no two of which differ by |·|. At a depth-zero place over Q_g, a solvable base change makes
the component a principal series of that kind (
thm-depth-zero-base-change-principal-series), and restricting to the smaller Galois
group does not change inertia. Where the definition asks only for the dimension of the
Weil–Deligne representation, there is nothing to prove.

text.tspan: 3. Geometric Galois representations in odd rank

svg.text: This section supplies the first input of sec-gal-assembly. We move an automorphic
representation of the definite unitary group U_a, a odd, with a cuspidal type at one place
above l and lacunary weights at another, to a Hecke eigensystem on a compact unitary
Shimura variety of signature (1, a-1) (thm-transfer-unitary-shimura). The Kuga–Sato
varieties over it (sec-gal-kuga-sato) and the results on Hecke eigenspaces (
sec-gal-eigenspaces) give a Galois representation of unknown dimension on which the
This section is general étale cohomology, with no unitary groups. For a smooth projective
variety with finite étale Hecke correspondences, each system of Hecke eigenvalues cuts out a
congruence relation at a place of good reduction controls Frobenius; a good model above l
makes the representation crystalline; and the Hodge–Tate decomposition, which commutes
with the correspondences, gives Hodge–Tate weights from Hodge numbers. The classical
inputs (proper base change, the projective bundle formula, finiteness) come first.

text.tspan: 5. Kuga-Sato varieties over unitary Shimura varieties

svg.text: This section shows that the Kuga–Sato varieties over compact unitary Shimura varieties of
signature (1, n-1), the fibre powers of the universal abelian scheme, satisfy the hypotheses
smoothness and good reduction come from the integral models of sec-gal-shimura-models
. The Hodge numbers of their eigenspaces come from the holomorphic Lefschetz formula:
fixed points of Hecke correspondences are CM points, and the sum over them is a sum of

text.tspan: 6. Integral models of compact unitary Shimura varieties

svg.text: The Kuga–Sato varieties of sec-gal-kuga-sato live over integral models of unitary Shimura
varieties of Harris–Taylor type. This section proves, after Kottwitz, that the moduli problem is
represented by a quasi-projective scheme, smooth of relative dimension a(n-1) (
thm-unitary-shimura-integral-models). Smoothness comes from counting first-order
deformations through the eigenparts of de Rham homology.

text.tspan: 7. Base change between definite unitary groups and GL(n)

svg.text: sec-gal-assembly passes between definite unitary groups and GL_n over CM fields by base
change. This section states weak base change in isobaric form (thm-base-change-unitary,
after Labesse) and in the form with local components (thm-labesse-base-change). It also
gives the local results behind the comparison of trace formulas: a bound for Hecke operators,
from wave kernels on GL_n(ℂ) and the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma; a twisted trace on
the lowest type at the archimedean places; and the Leibniz rule for Bernstein–Zelevinsky

text.tspan: 8. The forms used by the families

svg.text: thm-grh-from-theta-integrals uses thm-galois-reps-polarized in two forms,
recorded here. By the Gelfand–Kazhdan theorem a conjugate self-dual cuspidal
representation forms a polarized pair, so it has a Galois representation; in the abelian case
this is compatible above l as well (thm-galois-reps-csd-above-l). The second form
states the polarization through the inverse transpose (
